In a bright white show space inside the Garde Republicaine, the sprawling barracks of Paris' mounted gendarmes, guests including actors Sofia Vergara and Emmy Rossum fanned themselves on an unusually warm and sunny October day. The collection had splashes of colour, too, with a billowing parka in bright orange worn over a knit mini dress, and a zipped skirt in what Vanhée called sunflower yellow, paired with a matching high-collared jacket. Vanhée has been womenswear creative director since 2014 for Hermes, which caters to the ultra-wealthy and tightly controls access to its products, with years-long waiting lists for its most exclusive handbags. She will present the first haute couture collection for the brand in January. Hermes is one of many major luxury brands showing at Paris Fashion Week, which started on Monday and runs through October 6, with Chanel and Louis Vuitton runway shows still to come. The group is grappling with a slowdown in demand for luxury handbags and clothes and its shares are down 39% since the start of this year.

item.title: Ucrânia atacará refinarias russas em resposta à "nova doutrina" de ataques aéreos de Moscou
item.description: A Ucrânia intensificará os ataques às refinarias de petróleo russas em resposta a uma nova política de ataques aéreos de Moscou, destinada a forçar as pessoas a abandonarem Kiev e outras cidades, mas não terá como alvo civis, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: A Ucrânia intensificará os ataques às refinarias de petróleo russas em resposta a uma nova política de ataques aéreos de Moscou, destinada a forçar as pessoas a abandonarem Kiev e outras cidades, mas não terá como alvo civis, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy. A inteligência ucraniana obteve documentos que mostram que o líder russo, Vladimir Putin, havia emitido uma "nova doutrina" de ataques militares contra uma gama muito mais ampla de alvos civis antes deste inverno, disse Zelenskiy. "Vimos os documentos e sabemos que eles permitem que ataquem infraestrutura... logística... estradas, escolas, hospitais, para pressionar as pessoas a deixarem a capital e outras cidades", disse Zelenskiy. "Esse é o objetivo da operação." O que impulsionou a mudança na política, disse Zelenskiy, foi o desejo de Putin de parecer forte em um momento em que suas forças armadas estavam perdendo terreno em uma região-chave da linha de frente e sofrendo um número maior de baixas. O Kremlin não se pronunciou no sábado. Mas, em comunicado instando cidadãos estrangeiros a deixarem Kiev, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia afirmou que Moscou continuaria a atingir sistematicamente alvos no que chamou de ataques retaliatórios aos ataques ucranianos contra a Rússia nos últimos meses. Ambos os lados negam ter como alvo deliberadamente civis. CONTRATAQUE NO DONBAS Zelenskiy afirmou que uma contraofensiva ucraniana em andamento, de codinome “Vivaldi”, havia recapturado cerca de 140 km² (54 milhas quadradas) da região de Donbas, no leste da Ucrânia, que a Rússia afirma que deve controlar em sua totalidade como condição para qualquer acordo de paz. Nas últimas semanas, o governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, tem buscado retomar as negociações para pôr fim ao conflito que já dura quatro anos -- o mais sangrento da Europa desde a Segunda Guerra Mundial. No mês passado, o líder norte-americano instou a Ucrânia a evitar ataques a instalações petrolíferas russas, alegando que isso estava provocando uma alta nos preços globais do diesel. Mas Zelenskiy, falando enquanto sirenes de ataque aéreo soavam do lado de fora dos salões dourados dos escritórios presidenciais, disse não ter recebido nenhuma indicação da Rússia de que Putin estivesse interessado em negociações de paz ou em discutir um cessar-fogo em relação à infraestrutura energética. Na última semana, a capital ucraniana sofreu ataques persistentes de drones e mísseis russos contra ativos de energia e telecomunicações, além de infraestrutura rodoviária e ferroviária. Pela primeira vez, a Rússia atacou as pontes sobre o rio Dnipro que ligam o leste ao oeste de Kiev. Zelenskiy afirmou que a Ucrânia responderia à mudança de tática de Moscou, mas não retaliaria atacando infraestruturas civis indiscriminadamente.

item.title: ATP roundup: Carlos Alcaraz fights off 4 set points in Tokyo
item.description: Top-seeded Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz fought off four set points in the opener Saturday before rolling past Italy's Matteo Arnaldi to reach the Japan Open Tennis Championship quarterfinals in Tokyo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top-seeded Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz fought off four set points in the opener Saturday before rolling past Italy's Matteo Arnaldi to reach the Japan Open Tennis Championship quarterfinals in Tokyo. Alcaraz completed the 7-6 (6), 6-1 victory in one hour and 46 minutes. He trailed 6-2 in the tiebreaker before winning six straight points, then carried the momentum into the second set by winning the first five games. Alcaraz's quarterfinal opponent will be Canadian Denis Shapovalov, a 7-5, 3-6, 6-4 winner against Chile's Alejandro Tabilo. Czech Jiri Lehecka also advanced in three sets against Frenchman Ugo Humbert and will take on Paraguayan qualifier Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, who saved all three break points in a 7-6 (6), 6-1 win over Italian Matteo Berrettini. The other quarterfinal matchups are France's Kyrian Jacquet vs. Spain's Jaume Munar, and No. 8 Valentin Vacherot of Monaco vs. France's Arthur Fils. China Open No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev of Germany moved into the quarterfinals in Beijing with a 6-0, 6-3 victory in 55 minutes against Chinese hopeful Juncheng Shang. Zverev struck nine aces, never faced a break point and converted four of his five break chances to set up a showdown with sixth-seeded Serbian Novak Djokovic. Djokovic is a six-time champion with a perfect 31-0 record in this tournament. Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo advanced with a 6-3, 6-3 win over eighth-seeded Czech Jakub Mensik. Up next is No. 3 seed Daniil Medvedev of Russia, who had 10 aces in a 6-4, 6-3 victory against Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff. No. 5 Alex de Minaur of Australia and Russia's Andrey Rublev will meet in the quarterfinals after posting three-set triumphs. Rublev outlasted compatriot Roman Safiullin 6-2, 3-6, 6-4, and de Minaur rallied past Frenchman Quentin Halys 3-6, 7-6 (5), 7-5 in two hours and 47 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil tame India in 4-0 friendly win
item.description: Samuel Lino scored his first two goals for Brazil as India's frantic effort to hold off the five-time world champions faded after a spirited start, allowing the visitors to cruise to a 4-0 win in a friendly on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: Samuel Lino scored his first two goals for Brazil as India's frantic effort to hold off the five-time world champions faded after a spirited start, allowing the visitors to cruise to a 4-0 win in a friendly on Saturday. Chelsea winger Estevao scored Brazil's first goal and assisted Pedro before Lino netted a second-half brace, helping Carlo Ancelotti's side conclude their tour of Australia and India with two wins and a draw. Ancelotti, who has experimented with the squad throughout the three friendlies, made eight changes from Tuesday's 4-2 win over Australia, retaining only Vinicius Jr, Danilo and Gabriel Bontempo. India's strategy of leaving Vinicius unmarked on the left and trapping him offside had some early success as they combined their defenders with a low midfield to hold Brazil off, and targeted lone forward Manvir Singh with long balls. But Estevao delivered the breakthrough in the 28th minute, cutting in from the right to dispatch a left-footer at the near post, before setting up Brazil's second with a defence-splitting pass for Pedro to finish. Pedro set up Samuel Lino for the third goal near the hour mark, before the 26-year-old Flamengo winger dribbled past two defenders to make it 4-0 just before fulltime, as the crowd of 51,000 at the Salt Lake Stadium [USN:L6N45O0MC TEXT:"cheered the visitors"] as vocally as their own country. India, ranked 138th in the world, were left ruing their missed chances as Manvir and Ryan Williams failed to net a consolation goal, extending their winless streak to six matches.

item.title: Report: Packers star Micah Parsons likely out until November
item.description: Green Bay Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons is continuing his recovery from a torn ACL and is not likely to see game action until November.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Green Bay Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons is continuing his recovery from a torn ACL and is not likely to see game action until November. That's according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, who said Parsons has not had any setbacks. But the three-time All-Pro, who suffered a season-ending torn ACL on Dec. 14 in a game against the Denver Broncos, is less than 10 months into the recovery from the knee injury and subsequent surgery. Parsons, 27, is on the physically unable to perform list. The Packers were rolling at 9-3-1 entering the game where Parsons got injured, then went 0-4 to close the 2025 regular season and were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the Chicago Bears. The 2026 Packers certainly could use a healthy Parsons. Green Bay is 1-2 and sitting last in the NFC North. The Jordan Love-led offense has scored just 56 points, and opponents have scored 91 points for an NFC-worst differential of minus-35 points. The Packers have yet to open the 21-day practice window for Parsons, a five-time Pro Bowl selection who signed a four-year, $186 million extension with Green Bay after being acquired in an August 2025 trade with the Dallas Cowboys. Should he return in November, the Packers have games at the New England Patriots (Nov. 8), at home against the Minnesota Vikings (Nov. 15) and at the Los Angeles Rams for a Thanksgiving Eve game (Nov. 25). --Field Level Media

item.title: Rybakina's first match as world number one ends in China Open defeat by Charaeva
item.description: Three-times Grand Slam champion Elena Rybakina crashed out of the China Open with a shock 3-6 6-4 6-3 defeat by unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round on Saturday, marking a disappointing start to her reign as world number one.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three-times Grand Slam champion Elena Rybakina crashed out of the China Open with a shock 3-6 6-4 6-3 defeat by unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round on Saturday, marking a disappointing start to her reign as world number one. The 27-year-old was playing for the first time since defeating four-times major winner Aryna Sabalenka to capture the [USN:L1N45406M TEXT:"U.S. Open"] title last month. Rybakina had skipped Kazakhstan's Billie Jean King Cup Finals campaign after what she described as a [USN:L4N45A0XH TEXT:"physically demanding"] month. Charaeva, a 24-year-old Russian-born Armenian ranked 118th in the world, etched her name into the record books by becoming the lowest-ranked competitor since the introduction of the WTA rankings in 1975 to rally from a set down to defeat the world's top ranked player. Having weathered Rybakina's early charge, Charaeva converted five of eight break-point opportunities and won 76% of points behind her first serve. Rybakina struggled on serve, committing seven double faults in the two-hour, 11-minute contest at the WTA 1000 hardcourt event. Charaeva will next meet Britain's Sonay Kartal. In the men's draw, German top seed Alexander Zverev swept aside local hope Shang Juncheng 6-0 6-3 in the round of 16. Fresh from his [USN:L6N4550DD TEXT:"U.S. Open"] triumph and helping Team Europe win the [USN:L1N45J04Y TEXT:"Laver Cup"], Zverev will next take on 24-times Grand Slam champion [USN:L4N45O15G TEXT:"Novak Djokovic"] in Sunday's quarter-final. The 39-year-old Serb boasts a perfect 31-0 record at the ATP 500 event and holds the tournament record with six China Open titles.

item.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes
item.description: Ukrainian intelligence has documents showing that Vladimir Putin called for military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian intelligence has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said. "We saw documents and we know that they allow them attack infrastructure ... logistics ... roads, schools, hospitals, to pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities," Zelenskiy said. "This is the goal of the operation." Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties. The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians. COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said an ongoing Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region, which Russia has said it must control in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal. In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two. The US leader last month urged Ukraine to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations, saying that was sending global diesel prices surging. But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv. Zelenskiy said Ukraine would respond to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not respond in kind by targeting civilian infrastructure indiscriminately. "We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects." SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin to attend a G20 summit in Miami in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace. Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas. "It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for peace, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy." While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had not been set. Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time. Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defences have struggled as its previous generation of interceptor drones were too slow to catch them. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low. Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds. Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%. "We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way." BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile – the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles). Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish quickly a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow. "I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure." Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to divide support for Ukraine. Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had found funding to proceed with orders for drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian officials had worked on a plan with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year. The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said.

item.title: La Russie continuera à pilonner Kyiv, invite les diplomates à quitter la capitale ukrainienne
item.description: La Russie a déclaré samedi qu'elle continuerait à mener des frappes sur Kyiv et d'autres villes ukrainiennes, exhortant les ressortissants étrangers et les diplomates à quitter la capitale ukrainienne.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Russie a déclaré samedi qu'elle continuerait à mener des frappes sur Kyiv et d'autres villes ukrainiennes, exhortant les ressortissants étrangers et les diplomates à quitter la capitale ukrainienne. "En réponse aux actes terroristes commis par les forces armées ukrainiennes contre la population civile et les infrastructures civiles de notre pays, les forces armées de la Fédération de Russie continuent de mener systématiquement des frappes ciblées contre des installations militaires à Kyiv et dans d'autres villes ukrainiennes", a déclare le ministère russe des Affaires étrangères. "Le ministère russe des Affaires étrangères met une nouvelle fois en garde les ressortissants étrangers, y compris le personnel des missions diplomatiques, contre le fait de rester en Ukraine ou de se rendre sur son territoire." "La responsabilité de toute conséquence fâcheuse incombe entièrement à ceux qui ignorent cet avertissement", a déclaré le ministère. Ces déclarations interviennent après que des gouverneurs de régions ukrainiennes sous contrôle russe ont fait état de trois morts. Une personne a été tuée et dix autres blessées dans une attaque de drones à Zaporijjia, dans le sud-est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur nommé par Moscou dans cette région en partie sous contrôle des autorités russes, cité par l'agence de presse publique Tass. A Louhansk, une autre région dans l'est de l'Ukraine contrôlée en partie par la Russie, deux personnes ont été tuées et trois autres blessées lors d'attaques de drones, a déclaré le chef de la région nommé par la Russie. Dans la région russe de Belgorod, frontalière avec l'Ukraine, l'agence Tass a rapporté samedi qu'une personne a été tuée et deux autres blessées lors d'une attaque ukrainienne. Reuters n'a pas pu vérifier dans l'immédiat de manière indépendante ces informations. Depuis la fin de l’été, la Russie lance presque quotidiennement des dizaines de drones à réaction, rapides et relativement peu coûteux, contre l'Ukraine, dont les défenses peinent à faire face à cette nouvelle menace. A l'approche de l'hiver et comme il y a un an, les frappes russes visent notamment le réseau énergétique ukrainien. L'Ukraine va [USN:L6N45P05R TEXT:"intensifier"] ses attaques contre les raffineries russes en réponse à la nouvelle stratégie de frappes aériennes menée par Moscou visant à forcer la population à quitter Kyiv et d'autres villes, sans pour autant prendre pour cible les civils, a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.

item.title: Netherlands coach Xavi joins critics of new-look international window
item.description: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez has joined the criticism of the new-look expanded international calendar, saying four Nations League matches in 11 days are filled with peril.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez has joined the criticism of the new-look expanded international calendar, saying four Nations League matches in 11 days are filled with peril. Instead of two international games across nine days in each of September and October, FIFA has this year combined the two international windows into one with four match days, making for an intense programme. “This schedule is not good. Not for the national teams and not for the clubs that release their players and sometimes see them return injured,” Xavi told a press conference- on Saturday. The Dutch have 23 fit players for the Group A2 game against Serbia in Eindhoven on Sunday, with Brian Brobbey, Lutsharel Geertruida, Cody Gakpo and Jan Paul van Hecke all injured in their last three games and back at their clubs. “Scheduling such a packed calendar three months after the World Cup is asking for trouble,” Xavi added. “You also have training, travelling, recovering from matches and things like that. It’s very strange to schedule an international window like this at this stage of the season.” Spaniard Xavi, who was appointed Netherlands coach in August, suggested that authorities review the situation. “I would rather see us play two internationals," he said. "That would be better for everyone. But as far as I know, it was decided a long time ago that we will also have a block of four matches at this stage next year.” NEW INTERNATIONAL WINDOW POSES CHALLENGE The longer international window was always going to be a challenge for national team coaches, without any experience of how to handle the extra workload. Germany’s new coach Juergen Klopp called up 44 players in two separate squads, although the team's results have been mixed. “The shifts in training, work style, and play style between the national team and club inherently create certain risks. This format only heightens those risks rather than alleviating them,” England manager Thomas Tuchel said this week. Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente aired his opinion last month: "I don't like the new format; I prefer the old one. It gave you more rest. In my opinion, it took better care of the players' health,” he said. The next three international windows in November, March, and June will be the usual nine-day period with two match days, but FIFA has scheduled a combined September/October window of 16 days for the next four years, through to 2030.

item.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
item.description: A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Jana Winter, Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. Saif al-Din Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities, the three sources said. Two of them said he was brought into custody on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the circumstances of Khader’s detention or where he is being held. Two sources said that he is helping the FBI and global law enforcement locate the other hackers in the group. The FBI declined to comment on any specific arrest or activity abroad but said that the bureau "continues to aggressively investigate the recent cyber incident allegedly involving ShinyHunters, having already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects — and we will spare no resource in bringing each of the responsible individuals to justice." Reuters’ attempts to reach Khader and members of his family over the past week and a half have been unsuccessful. The detention of Khader — whose alleged hacker nickname is Rey — is the latest twist in the case of ShinyHunters. The prolific cyber extortion group, which has a long history of targeting major corporations around the world, is believed by experts to consist mainly of young, English-speaking hackers focused on data theft and extortion. Their theft of what they claim are mountains of data on every single FBI employee has drawn comparisons to the allegedly Chinese-linked intrusion at the US Office of Personnel Management in 2015, which compromised sensitive details on millions of Americans who had been vetted for security clearances. SENSITIVE INFORMATION A Reuters [USN:L6N45F0ZI TEXT:"analysis"] of a sample of the data shared by ShinyHunters revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information of FBI employees, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information. Khader's cooperation with investigators could be critical to helping contain -- or at least understand -- the damage. One source said he was walking investigators through his electronic devices and digital correspondence to help the FBI locate his cohorts. "His cooperation is critical to ongoing efforts to arrest these hackers," the source told Reuters. There have been hints for days that ShinyHunters was experiencing disruption following the announcement of its break-in at the FBI. Beginning on Tuesday, Reuters was unable to reach ShinyHunters through the online account it previously used to communicate with journalists. Then, on Wednesday, the group’s dark web site, where it had previously posted threats to the FBI, [USN:L6N45M1CE TEXT:"disappeared"]. FBI Director Kash Patel had been hinting at more arrests following [USN:S8N42N0JB TEXT:"the announcement"] that another alleged ShinyHunters member, Pepijn van der Stap, had been detained in the Netherlands. “FBI teams are working new leads RIGHT NOW,” Patel said on Wednesday in a message posted to X. “More arrests are on the table.” The operators of a ShinyHunters-linked email address did not respond to a request for comment on Friday. The operators of that email account previously told Reuters that the group’s site had gone offline due to sabotage from rivals and "disruption due to an unrelated incident." The group had previously struck a defiant note, saying on September 22 that it had hacked the FBI in retaliation over an advisory that accused ShinyHunters of making "exaggerated claims of access" to extort victims for money. It gave the FBI a week to withdraw the advisory. But in the most recent email to Reuters, the operators struck a conciliatory tone, saying that “we want no further escalation” with the FBI. The operators said Reuters could interpret their message as meaning, “ShinyHunters backing down completely.” KHADER'S IDENTITY LONG KNOWN Khader’s identity, and his alleged connection to ShinyHunters, have long been known to security researchers. Last year, the independent journalist Brian Krebs reported that Khader was a key member of Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters, an umbrella group of hackers that included ShinyHunters. Krebs, who said he spoke to Khader over Signal, quoted the teenager as saying he had quit the world of data breaches and extortion and was cooperating with law enforcement. But ShinyHunters continued its hacking spree into 2026, claiming credit for break-ins at [USN:L6N40W1A9 TEXT:"video game developer Rockstar Games"], the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion involving [USN:L6N41P0Z6 TEXT:"education tool Canvas"] that caused widespread disruption [USN:L6N41L0UT TEXT:"across US schools"]. Law enforcement agencies around the world, including in the United States, have struggled to arrest and prosecute members of related groups such as Lapsus$ or Scattered Spider, [USN:L1N3CE2RM TEXT:"Reuters has previously reported"]. Sources told Reuters that the difficulty stems from the hackers’ young ages, which can make prosecutions complex, or because the groups they belong to are so chaotic and informal, or because victims of their extortion attempts often decline to help investigators.

item.title: OF Aaron Judge (calf) left off Yankees' ALDS roster
item.description: Captain Aaron Judge was left off the New York Yankees' roster for their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Captain Aaron Judge was left off the New York Yankees' roster for their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees revealed their 26-man roster for the best-of-five series on Saturday morning, with Game 1 set for 6:38 p.m. ET in St. Petersburg, Fla. Judge, 34, has not played since Sept. 16 with a strained right calf. The three-time league MVP landed on the injured list three days later and missed the Yankees' two-game wild-card sweep against the rival Boston Red Sox earlier this week. Judge faced live pitching for the first time since the injury on Monday, was running in the outfield on Tuesday and took batting practice on Wednesday and Thursday. The outfielder participated in workouts on Friday at the Yankees' minor league facility in Tampa and also at Tropicana Field. Judge has voiced his determination to return in the postseason, but the team ultimately decided to move forward without him against Tampa Bay. Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos and Giancarlo Stanton are the outfielders on the ALDS roster set to face the Rays. Cody Bellinger and Jose Caballero, who can play in both the infield and outfield, are listed as utility players. Judge largely was ineffective before the calf injury, batting .174 (4-for-23) with a homer and three RBIs in seven games after his Sept. 8 return from the injured list. He had missed more than three months with a fractured rib. In 66 games overall this year, Judge batted .241 with a .360 on-base percentage, a .511 slugging percentage, 18 homers and 41 RBIs. That is the fewest number of games Judge has played since his 2016 debut season, not including the 2020 pandemic campaign. An eight-time All-Star and three-time American League MVP, Judge still is looking for his first World Series championship. He is a career .236 hitter in the postseason with 17 home runs and 41 RBIs in 65 games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tunisia's Esperance appoint Spaniard Franco as coach
item.description: Esperance have appointed Spanish coach Pablo Franco as their head coach, the Tunisian club said on Saturday, entrusting the 46-year-old with the task of reclaiming the league title after he guided Morocco's Maghreb Fez to their first championship in 41 years last season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Esperance have appointed Spanish coach Pablo Franco as their head coach, the Tunisian club said on Saturday, entrusting the 46-year-old with the task of reclaiming the league title after he guided Morocco's Maghreb Fez to their first championship in 41 years last season. The Spaniard replaces Romanian Laurențiu Reghecampf, whose second spell in charge ended after four matches with Esperance top of the Tunisian league standings. Reghecampf, 51, led the side to three wins in four games following his return to the club this season. Franco arrives in Tunis after leading Maghreb Fez to their first Moroccan league crown since 1985. The Moroccan club, however, parted ways with him in July with local media attributing the split either to the Spaniard's desire for a new challenge or to broader changes within the club's sporting structure.

item.title: Ex-Yale football coach Tony Reno dies at 52
item.description: Tony Reno, who led Yale's football team to five Ivy League titles, died at age 52.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tony Reno, who led Yale's football team to five Ivy League titles, died at age 52. Yale announced his passing on Friday. Reno, who took over the program in 2012, had a career record of 83-49 at the time he announced his resignation in February due to health issues. Yale did not announce his cause of death, but the Hartford Courant reported Reno had been diagnosed with a neurodegenerative disease in August 2025. Last fall, he led the team to its first FCS playoff berth. He helped Yale overcome a 28-point deficit in the second half of a 43-42 victory over Youngstown State in the first round before the team fell to eventual national champion Montana State in the second. Reno's tenure also included seven wins in his last nine meetings against archrival Harvard. Reno was a coach known for teaching players about both football and life. "As a coach, Tony loved his players and held them to a standard they often didn't know they were capable of reaching," said Kevin Cahill, who succeeded Reno. "He was hard on them and demanding, but every day, they knew he cared about them. It was never about him or simply about winning championships; it was about developing young men and leaders and helping them become the best versions of themselves. "Along the way, we won a lot of football games. Tony will be missed dearly. His impact on so many lives will never be forgotten, and his legacy will forever be a part of the Yale Football family." Reno was an assistant coach for more than a decade before being named head coach. He was Ivy League Coach of the Year in 2022. "Coach Reno understood something generations of us who played at Yale know deeply: Yale Football transforms young men's lives", said Patrick A. Ruwe, M.D., who is the president of the Yale Football Association. "That transformation isn't a tradition -- it's the purpose. He was an extraordinary coach, but his real legacy is how he deepened that purpose -- teaching discipline, resilience, accountability, and leadership, and creating opportunities that changed the trajectory of his players' lives." Reno is survived by his wife, Toni, and children Dante, Angelina and Vince. Dante Reno is the starting quarterback for the Bulldogs. Yale (1-1) is scheduled to play Merrimack on Saturday at noon at the Yale Bowl in New Haven, Conn. --Field Level Media

item.title: Espagne Des dizaines de milliers de personnes manifestent contre la crise du logement
item.description: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes manifestent samedi dans les rues de Madrid et d'autres villes espagnoles pour dénoncer une crise du logement, leur colère étant exacerbée après le rejet par le Parlement d'une série de mesures proposées par le gouvernement socialiste censées juguler cette crise.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes manifestent samedi dans les rues de Madrid et d'autres villes espagnoles pour dénoncer une crise du logement, leur colère étant exacerbée après le [USN:L8N45O138 TEXT:"rejet"] par le Parlement d'une série de [USN:L6N45L0P2 TEXT:"mesures proposées"] par le gouvernement socialiste censées juguler cette crise. Le mouvement ne cesse de prendre de l'ampleur depuis le 23 septembre, jour où la police a [USN:L6N45K0I9 TEXT:"expulsé"] sur une civière Maricarmen Abascal, 87 ans, de son logement madrilène qu'elle occupait depuis plus de sept décennies, en vertu d'un arrêté d'expulsion obtenu par le fonds d'investissement qui avait racheté son appartement. Parmi les banderoles brandies par les manifestants figure notamment un appel à la grève générale en raison de la situation immobilière. A titre d'exemple, les loyers ont doublé au cours de la dernière décennie, les tarifs moyens atteignant 1.176 euros par mois, soit 98,7% du salaire moyen d'un jeune, selon le Conseil de la jeunesse d'Espagne. "C'est une honte", a déclaré Nando de Anguulo, 26 ans, au sujet des rejet des mesures proposées par le gouvernement de gauche. Ce dernier ne dispose par d'une majorité au Parlement. "Cela ne fait que prouver que c'est nous, les citoyens, qui devons nous adapter aux partis politiques, et non les politiciens aux attentes de la population, et cela ne peut pas continuer ainsi", a-t-elle ajouté Le président du gouvernement espagnol Pedro Sanchez pourrait convoquer des élections anticipées en novembre après l'échec de l'adoption de ces mesures relatives au logement, ont rapporté vendredi les médias espagnols. Le cabinet de Pedro Sanchez a refusé de commenter ces informations.

item.title: Taiwan women's tennis feud flares up at Asian Games
item.description: "At the US Open, I didn’t shake her hand, and that’s because in previous times I didn’t get any response and I felt that there was no point in sticking my warm face to a cold butt," Chan Hao-ching said of Hsieh Su-wei.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Taiwanese tennis players Hsieh Su-wei and Chan Hao-ching revived their feud at the Asian Games on Saturday, with Chan fuming at Hsieh for a handshake snub at the end of their women's doubles final in Nagoya. The pair did not shake hands following a[USN:L1N45002J TEXT:" tense US Open doubles match"] where Hsieh's playing partner Jelena Ostapenko roared at Chan's coach in the player's box after sealing victory. The Taiwanese rivals later traded barbs on social media about the incident. Chan on Saturday said she had been willing to put all that behind her after she and Wu Fang-hsien lost 6-4 4-6 (10-5) to Hsieh and Liang En-shuo in an all-Taiwan clash for the doubles gold at Higashiyama Park Tennis Center. "At the US Open, I didn’t shake her hand, and that’s because in previous times I didn’t get any response and I felt that there was no point in sticking my warm face to a cold butt," said the 33-year-old. "But today, I felt this is a match for (Taiwan). Before the match, I decided that I would stretch out my hand after the match. But I still didn’t get to shake her hand." Chan said she was also disappointed during the tiebreak when Taiwan's head tennis coach clapped for Hsieh. "At that moment, I felt quite down. After all, his role today is the head coach," said Chan, who won the doubles gold at the Hangzhou Asian Games three years ago. Hsieh, a nine-times Grand Slam champion in doubles, played down the handshake snub. “It’s important to respect your opponents on court," the 40-year-old said. "If my opponent doesn’t respect me, what’s there to say? I wouldn’t feel like shaking hands, that’s it.”

item.title: Ventaja de Lula sobre Bolsonaro se reduce de cara a las elecciones en Brasil: encuesta CNT/MDA
item.description: La ventaja del presidente brasileño Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sobre el senador Flávio Bolsonaro se ha reducido de cara a la primera vuelta de las elecciones del domingo, según reveló el sábado una encuesta de CNT/MDA, que también apunta a una contienda más reñida en un probable balotaje.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La ventaja del presidente brasileño Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sobre el senador Flávio Bolsonaro se ha reducido de cara a la primera vuelta de las elecciones del domingo, según reveló el sábado una encuesta de CNT/MDA, que también apunta a una contienda más reñida en un probable balotaje. En un escenario de primera vuelta, Lula obtendría el 43,1% de los votos, seguido de Bolsonaro con el 38%. Más atrás aparecen los candidatos Augusto Cury (3,2%), Ronaldo Caiado (3%) y Renan Santos (1,5%), según el sondeo. Una encuesta del 15 de septiembre situaba a Lula en un 40,5%, a Bolsonaro en un 30,4%, a Cury en un 6%, a Caiado en un 3% y a Santos en un 2,7%. Teniendo en cuenta únicamente los votos válidos previstos, lo que excluye a quienes indicaron a la empresa encuestadora que dejarían su papeleta en blanco o la anularían de algún modo, Lula alcanzó un 47,8% de apoyo electoral frente al 42,1% de Bolsonaro. Si ningún candidato obtiene más del 50% de los votos válidos en la primera vuelta del domingo, los dos postulantes más votados pasarán a una segunda vuelta, que se celebrará el 25 de octubre. En un probable balotaje, Lula obtendría un 47,3% de apoyo electoral, frente al 43,1% del hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, según la encuesta. En el sondeo anterior, Lula aventajaba al senador Bolsonaro por un 47,3% frente a un 40% en la segunda vuelta. MDA encuestó a 2.007 personas entre el 30 de septiembre y el 2 de octubre, con un margen de error del 2,2 puntos porcentuales.

item.title: Inflación de Venezuela en septiembre cierra en 8,4%: Banco Central
item.description: La inflación de Venezuela en septiembre cerró en 8,4% una leve desaceleración respecto a agosto cuando fue 8,9%, según los datos divulgados el sábado por el Banco Central.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La inflación de Venezuela en septiembre cerró en 8,4% una leve desaceleración respecto a agosto cuando fue 8,9%, según los datos divulgados el sábado por el Banco Central. Con los indicadores de septiembre, la inflación anualizada se ubicó en 465,5%, según cálculos de Reuters basados en las cifras del Banco Central (BCV). La inflación acumulada en nueve meses de este año fue 225,3%. El BCV dijo que la estabilización en el mercado cambiario incidió en el dato de septiembre. "La normalización de los flujos de ingresos externos hacia la economía nacional y el descenso de las presiones cambiarias, han motivado a que el tipo de cambio muestre un comportamiento hacia la estabilización, repercutiendo no solo en una menor brecha cambiaria, sino también en una menor variación de los precios de los bienes y servicios", agregó el comunicado.

item.title: Copiloto de flydubai atacó al piloto con un hacha en intento de "ataque terrorista", según EAU
item.description: El copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, con destino a Israel, intentó llevar a cabo un "ataque terrorista" con un hacha durante el vuelo, informó el sábado el fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Eman Abouhassira, Maha Dahan, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: El copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, con destino a Israel, intentó llevar a cabo un "ataque terrorista" con un hacha durante el vuelo, informó el sábado el fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. El copiloto fue identificado como Hammam al-Hammami, de nacionalidad omaní, informó a Reuters una fuente con conocimiento directo del asunto. Una segunda fuente al corriente de la investigación confirmó el nombre del copiloto. Las autoridades de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de confirmación de su identidad. Se evitó una catástrofe el miércoles después de que los pasajeros y la tripulación redujeran al copiloto, que había atacado al capitán en lo que, según las autoridades israelíes, fue un aparente intento de estrellar el avión, en el que viajaban más de 170 pasajeros y tripulantes. Aunque las autoridades emiratíes y la aerolínea no han identificado públicamente al copiloto, funcionarios israelíes habían afirmado anteriormente que se trata de un ciudadano omaní. Omán no se ha pronunciado sobre el incidente. "Las investigaciones sobre el incidente relacionado con el vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai revelaron que el copiloto había intentado llevar a cabo un ataque terrorista", dijo el fiscal general Hamad Saif Al Shamsi en un comunicado difundido por la agencia estatal de noticias de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. El copiloto atacó al piloto dentro de la cabina con un hacha de emergencia e intentó tomar el control de la aeronave, según el fiscal general. Normalmente, en la cabina se guarda un hacha de emergencia para su uso en situaciones de emergencia, como accidentes aéreos. La investigación sobre el vuelo FZ1073, incluidos los motivos del sospechoso, sigue en curso, y las conclusiones se darán a conocer una vez que se hayan completado los "trámites necesarios", señaló el fiscal general. Los Emiratos Árabes Unidos lideran la investigación. La aerolínea es propiedad del Gobierno de Dubái. MAYORÍA DE PASAJEROS ERAN ISRAELÍES Los comentarios del fiscal general fueron los primeros de los investigadores emiratíes en calificar el incidente como un intento de ataque terrorista. Tras la publicación de la declaración del fiscal general, Anwar Gargash, asesor principal del presidente de los EAU, dijo en X que el país del golfo tenía tolerancia cero con el terrorismo y no mostraría indulgencia alguna ante la retórica extremista. Flydubai dijo que las circunstancias que rodeaban el incidente aún se estaban investigando y que no estaba en condiciones de hacer más comentarios, dijo un portavoz el sábado. Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato las páginas profesionales y de redes sociales que, según se informa, pertenecen al copiloto, lo que sugería que había trabajado para otras aerolíneas. Royal Air Maroc respondió a Reuters, ante una pregunta sobre su posible empleo en la compañía en el pasado, que había realizado un curso de formación de tres meses con la aerolínea en 2025, pero que su solicitud para trabajar allí posteriormente fue rechazada. RAM no dio más detalles. En sus primeras declaraciones públicas sobre el incidente, el presidente ejecutivo de flydubai, Ghaith al Ghaith, dijo el viernes que el vuelo se desvió tras un "incidente de seguridad" en la cabina de mando. La mayoría de los pasajeros a bordo eran ciudadanos israelíes. Un piloto de reserva de flydubai que viajaba en el vuelo tomó el control de la aeronave y la aterrizó en el aeropuerto de Tabuk, en el noroeste de Arabia Saudita, donde el copiloto fue detenido por las autoridades sauditas . El copiloto fue trasladado desde Arabia Saudita a Abu Dabi el jueves. Una fuente informada sobre la investigación dijo el viernes a Reuters que se esperaba que funcionarios israelíes interrogaran al copiloto en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. La fuente se negó a precisar qué agencia o autoridad israelí participaría. Un funcionario del Gobierno israelí dijo que los investigadores israelíes participarían junto a las autoridades emiratíes en la investigación liderada por los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. Israel no mantiene relaciones diplomáticas oficiales con Omán, y el primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, ha declarado que no se permite a pilotos de esos países operar vuelos con destino a Israel. No estaba claro cómo el copiloto llegó a ser asignado al vuelo con destino a Tel Aviv. El viernes, Netanyahu dijo que Israel estaba investigando si el copiloto había actuado bajo las órdenes de alguien, y advirtió de que cualquier persona implicada pagaría un "alto precio". La aeronave descendió unos 16.625 pies en poco más de 30 segundos mientras sobrevolaba Arabia Saudita en su trayecto desde los Emiratos Árabes Unidos a Israel, según los datos de seguimiento de vuelos de Flightradar24. La ruta es muy popular entre los viajeros israelíes.

item.title: Lula's lead over Bolsonaro narrows ahead of Brazil vote, CNT/MDA poll shows
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro narrowed ahead of Sunday's first-round vote, a CNT/MDA poll showed on Saturday, while also pointing to a tighter race in a likely runoff.

item.title: Lula lidera por 47,8% a 42,1% contra Flávio nos votos válidos do 1º turno, diz CNT/MDA
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) está à frente do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa CNT/MDA divulgada neste sábado, véspera da eleição.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) está à frente do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa CNT/MDA divulgada neste sábado, véspera da eleição. O levantamento coloca o petista com 43,1% das intenções de voto contra 38% do senador. Na pesquisa anterior, divulgada no mês passado, Lula tinha 40% e Flávio somava 30%. Os demais candidatos somados chegam agora a 9%, ante 16% na pesquisa anterior. Brancos e nulos são 5%, ante 6%, e indecisos somam 5%, ante 8%. Nos votos válidos, quando são excluídos os brancos, nulos e indecisos, Lula tem 47,8% contra 42,1% de Flávio. Na pesquisa anterior, Lula tinha 47% e Flávio somava 35%. A soma dos demais candidatos agora é de 10%, ante 18% na pesquisa anterior. Para vencer a eleição no primeiro turno, um candidato precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos. Em um eventual segundo turno entre Lula e Flávio, que, se for necessário, acontecerá três semanas após a votação de domingo, no dia 25 de outubro, Lula aparece com 47,3% contra 43,1% de Flávio, o que significa um empate técnico dentro da margem de erro da pesquisa, que é de 2,2 pontos percentuais. No levantamento anterior, Lula tinha 47% e Flávio somava 40%. Brancos e nulos somam agora 8%, ante 10%, enquanto indecisos se mantiveram em 2%. Para a pesquisa, contratada pela Confederação Nacional do Transporte (CNT), o instituto MDA entrevistou 2.007 pessoas entre quarta e sexta-feira.

item.title: Fiscalía de Portugal investiga legalidad del uso de base de Lajes por parte de EEUU en la guerra de Irán
item.description: La Fiscalía portuguesa anunció el sábado que había abierto una investigación sobre la legalidad de la autorización concedida por el Gobierno de centro-derecha para que Estados Unidos utilizara la base aérea de Lajes, en las Azores, durante el conflicto con Irán, a raíz de una denuncia presentada por un partido de la oposición.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Fiscalía portuguesa anunció el sábado que había abierto una investigación sobre la legalidad de la autorización concedida por el Gobierno de centro-derecha para que Estados Unidos utilizara la base aérea de Lajes, en las Azores, durante el conflicto con Irán, a raíz de una denuncia presentada por un partido de la oposición. Un acuerdo de larga data con Estados Unidos permite a Washington utilizar la base sin autorización previa en tiempos de paz, pero exige que Portugal dé su aprobación una vez que comiencen las hostilidades. Portugal, a diferencia de la vecina España, autorizó varios vuelos de tránsito estadounidenses a través de la base aérea de Lajes, una decisión que suscitó críticas por parte de los partidos de la oposición de izquierdas y desencadenó un debate político sobre el papel de Lisboa en las operaciones relacionadas con el conflicto con Irán. En un comunicado, la Fiscalía General dijo que "la investigación se abrió a raíz de una denuncia presentada por miembros del partido Bloque de Izquierda", sin ofrecer más detalles. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Portugal se negó a hacer comentarios. El Bloque de Izquierda solicitó en abril a la fiscalía que investigara el uso de la base de Lajes por parte de Estados Unidos, argumentando que constituía una "grave violación del derecho internacional". Sin embargo, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, Paulo Rangel, ha afirmado que Portugal no estaba implicado en el conflicto y que el uso de la base de Lajes se ajustaba al derecho internacional, ya que se autorizó únicamente tras las garantías de Washington de que cualquier operación sería defensiva, necesaria y proporcionada, y se limitaría a objetivos militares. Los fiscales portugueses están sujetos al principio de legalidad, que les obliga a investigar presuntas irregularidades cuando existen motivos suficientes para hacerlo, a diferencia de lo que ocurre en algunas jurisdicciones, donde los fiscales disponen de una mayor discrecionalidad para decidir si un caso debe seguir adelante. La base de Lajes, situada en el archipiélago portugués de las Azores, en el Atlántico, es un centro estratégico de tránsito para las fuerzas estadounidenses en virtud de un tratado bilateral de defensa que data de 1951 y alberga la 65.ª Grupo de Base Aérea de la Fuerza Aérea de los Estados Unidos, que presta apoyo a las operaciones de Estados Unidos, la OTAN y sus aliados.

item.title: Exiled Russian filmmaker Zvyagintsev takes aim at Putin's war in Oscar bid
item.description: Exiled Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev takes on Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine in "Minotaur", a drama about conscription and moral compromise released nearly five years after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.
item.dc:creator: Michaela Cabrera
item.content:encoded: Exiled Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev takes on Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine in "Minotaur", a drama about conscription and moral compromise released nearly five years after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion. The film, which won the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival this year and is an entry for the 2027 Oscar for best international film, is released as debate persists over Russia's ability to sustain troop numbers in a conflict that has left hundreds of thousands dead or wounded. One scene shows Russian conscripts boarding a bus for the front, with a father saying goodbye to his teenage son, while the mother of another screams in anguish. Later, the image of an older recruit appears on a roadside billboard: he is dead and celebrated as a war hero. The story centres on Gleb, the owner of a logistics company who is coming to grips with his wife having an affair, while being pressured by the local mayor to identify 14 employees for military service. Unwilling to send his existing workers to the front, he recruits new drivers with promises of high salaries, only to dispatch them straight to the war. "For a director who has lived there, was born there, and speaks only Russian ... how could he not talk about what has become the main, if not the most important, event of recent years?" Zvyagintsev said of himself in an interview with Reuters. The 62-year-old director, best known internationally for "Leviathan" and "Loveless", both Oscar nominated, now lives in France, having left Russia in 2021, months before Moscow launched what it calls its special military operation in Ukraine. PROPAGANDA VERSUS SOFT POWER "Minotaur", produced in France, is in Russian but its topic means it will never be officially released in Russia. Zvyagintsev is sceptical anyway that it can shift opinion about the war. Support in Russia for the military campaign in Ukraine remained above 70% in 2026 polling by the Levada Center, although 67% of respondents also favoured peace negotiations. "Propaganda is like a heavy hammer, like pliers, like an anvil. It's a very crude instrument," he said. "Art, on the other hand, deals with subtleties. This soft power works over the long term." Moscow has avoided another compulsory mobilisation since its politically damaging 2022 call-up, relying instead on recruitment drives and signing bonuses, though some analysts say a fresh mobilisation cannot be ruled out. Videos of Russia's mobilisation campaigns posted online helped shape the screenplay, Zvyagintsev said. Unable to shoot in Russia, where he has not returned since suffering a severe bout of COVID-19 in 2021, he used a Latvian town as a stand-in. "I don't think that after 60 years of life experience a person can suddenly lose touch with reality in just one year," he said. Critics have described "Minotaur", which opens in French cinemas on October 14, as one of Zvyagintsev's most overt commentaries on Russia's political and moral condition. "This is all we could do: tell the story as we see it and find the human being in this unbearable state of compromise," he said. In August, Russia [USN:L8N45A15W TEXT:"designated"] Zvyagintsev a "foreign agent", a label applied to public figures accused by authorities of carrying out anti-Russian activities with foreign support. He declined to comment on what impact the designation might have on him personally or professionally. FROM CHABROL TO UKRAINE Zvyagintsev had originally sought to remake French director Claude Chabrol's 1969 thriller "La Femme Infidele" ("The Unfaithful Wife"), about a husband who suspects his wife is having an affair. But when the rights were finally secured and work on the screenplay began in 2022, Russia's invasion of Ukraine transformed the project. Chabrol's suburban Paris setting became a bleak Russian town, and the domestic tensions of the original story were recast against the backdrop of war. "I realise now that we were simply lucky that in 2018-2019 we weren't able to acquire the rights," he said. "If we had made the film in 2018, it would have been completely different."

item.title: Rusia promete continuar ataques masivos contra Kiev, insta a diplomáticos extranjeros abandonar la ciudad
item.description: Rusia dijo el sábado que seguiría llevando a cabo ataques de represalia selectivos contra Kiev y otras ciudades ucranianas, e instó a los ciudadanos extranjeros y a los diplomáticos a abandonar la capital.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rusia dijo el sábado que seguiría llevando a cabo ataques de represalia selectivos contra Kiev y otras ciudades ucranianas, e instó a los ciudadanos extranjeros y a los diplomáticos a abandonar la capital. En un comunicado, el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores ruso dijo que "en respuesta a los actos terroristas de las Fuerzas Armadas ucranianas contra la población civil y las infraestructuras civiles de nuestro país, las Fuerzas Armadas de la Federación Rusa siguen llevando a cabo de forma sistemática ataques selectivos contra instalaciones militares en Kiev y otras ciudades ucranianas". "El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia advierte una vez más a los ciudadanos extranjeros, incluido el personal de las misiones diplomáticas, que no permanezcan en Ucrania ni viajen a su territorio", agregó. "La responsabilidad de cualquier consecuencia adversa recae íntegramente en quienes ignoren esta advertencia", señaló el ministerio. Rusia ha intensificado recientemente los ataques contra infraestructuras de la capital ucraniana, alcanzando el sábado un puente sobre el río Dniéper en un ataque aéreo. La intensificación de la campaña ha trastornado la vida de los tres millones de habitantes de la capital de cara a los duros meses de invierno boreal. El presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, dijo esta semana que Ucrania estaba pagando el precio de sus propios ataques contra Rusia y que seguiría haciéndolo mientras las fuerzas de Moscú atacaran sistemáticamente diferentes objetivos en el país. Tanto Rusia como Ucrania han intensificado en los últimos meses los ataques contra los buques graneleros del bando contrario en el mar Negro, mientras que las refinerías de petróleo rusas y otras empresas siguen siendo blanco de los bombardeos ucranianos y los drones ucranianos matan a civiles en las regiones fronterizas rusas. Ambas partes niegan estar atacando a civiles o infraestructuras civiles.

item.title: France to step up Ebola funding in Congo amid resurgence fears, minister says
item.description: France will step up its support for efforts to eradicate Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Saturday during a visit to a region hit by the virus, warning that it could quickly resurge if vigilance waned.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France will step up its support for efforts to eradicate Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Saturday during a visit to a region hit by the virus, warning that it could quickly resurge if vigilance waned. * Barrot made rare trip by a Western leader to the northeastern Congolese city of [USN:L6N45H0UF TEXT:"Bunia"], where a laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in mid-September. * France allocated €13.4 million ($15.1 million) to the fight against Ebola between January and July. * Barrot said he would propose additional humanitarian funding for Ebola during upcoming French budget discussions. * France's response came through humanitarian aid, medical research and the PRISM programme launched during President Emmanuel Macron's 2023 visit. * A national humanitarian conference is to be held in Paris on October 6, during which Ebola is to be discussed. * "Ebola may seem far away to some people or political leaders, but it can return very quickly. Our responsibility is to prevent those resurgences," Barrot told reporters in Bunia. * Barrot praised Congolese authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian organisations and medical workers for containing the epidemic and preventing it from spreading to major urban centres in Congo and beyond. * "There is no need to fear or worry. First and foremost, we must fight the epidemic where it emerges," Barrot said when asked whether it could spread after a case was reported in France. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Blues eager to extend strong start in clash vs. Avalanche
item.description: The St. Louis Blues have started slowly in each of the past four seasons, but maybe this one will be different.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The St. Louis Blues have started slowly in each of the past four seasons, but maybe this one will be different. The Blues made a strong start on Friday, defeating the Dallas Stars 4-0 in the season opener. Now, the Blues have another task ahead of them as they visit the Colorado Avalanche on Saturday night in Denver. The last time the Blues posted a winning record in October was 2021, when they finished the month 6-1-0 and ended the season 49-22-11. They reached the playoffs just once since, a first-round exit in 2025, so the emphasis on starting strong is a priority for St. Louis. "I think it's important," Blues defenseman Philip Broberg said. "You don't want to chase, you want to get off to a good start and everybody feeling good about their game and being confident. I think a good start is important and just keep building from that. "I think every team talks about a good start. I think in the past we haven't really had really good starts, so I think we want to put an emphasis on making sure we prepare" for the opening games. Joel Hofer had 25 saves against the Stars on Friday night, so it likely will be Jordan Binnington in net against Colorado. Binnington played in just one of the three games against the Avalanche last season and allowed six goals on 43 shots in a 6-1 Colorado victory on New Year's Eve. While the Blues were battling in Dallas, the Avalanche were resting after opening the season with an 8-4 win over the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday night. Colorado provided plenty of offense, scoring four times on the power play, but it let in two short-handed goals, continuing a trend from last season. The Avalanche allowed an NHL-most 13 short-handed goals in 2025-26. "Weird that we obviously gave up a couple on the power play there, but we found a way to capitalize a couple more on our power play," defenseman Cale Makar said. "So trade off, but that can't happen." Colorado's roster for its opener included seven defensemen and 11 forwards, with blueliner Noah Juulsen getting some shifts on the fourth line. Head coach Jared Bednar likely will go with a more traditional lineup if winger Zachary L'Heureux is brought off injured reserve. L'Heureux and Fedor Svechkov were acquired from Nashville in a June deal that sent fellow forwards Jack Drury and Chase Bradley and a 2029 third-round draft pick to the Predators. L'Heureux has played in 87 NHL games over the last two seasons and is a physical player who can impact the game with that style. "I think I've had a lot of success playing that kind of rat style, in-your-face hockey while still bringing a lot of offense," L'Heureux said. The offense is led by Nathan MacKinnon, who had two goals against the Kings and added a rare fight in the third period. The Avalanche led the NHL in scoring last season with 298 goals and may need to be that prolific if the defense plays like it did in the opener. --Field Level Media

item.title: US to lend $4.2 billion to Vistra to boost nuclear power output, source says
item.description: The US will lend Vistra Corp about $4.2 billion to boost its nuclear power generation, a person familiar with the matter said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US will lend Vistra Corp (VST.N) about $4.2 billion to boost its nuclear power generation, a person familiar with the matter said on Saturday. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright will make the announcement on Monday at Vistra's nuclear plant along Lake Erie in Ohio, said the person, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. The loan would be used to boost power output, or "uprate" at least three of Vistra's four nuclear stations, which can be done without requiring new licenses from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The Department of Energy and Vistra did not immediately respond to requests for comment. According to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, utilities can uprate nuclear plants by refueling with slightly more enriched uranium, or a higher percentage of new fuel, or through major plant modifications such as the replacement of main turbines. Utilities since the 1970s have used uprates to generate more power from reactors, the NRC's website says. As of 2022 the agency had approved more than 170 uprates, according to the NRC. Vistra has six reactors at four US plants that generate more than 6.5 gigawatts of electricity, enough to power about 3.25 million homes. US power demand is growing for the first time in decades, driven by surging demand from the expansion of [USN:L6N44912S TEXT:"AI data centers"], electrification of transportation and cryptocurrency mining. President Donald Trump set a goal to quadruple US nuclear power capacity by 2050. The US Department of Energy has hundreds of billions of dollars in financing available from its loan office and Wright has said the [USN:L1N3WM0OV TEXT:"bulk of that"] loan capacity will support nuclear power plants. The Vistra news was first reported by Bloomberg. (This story has been refiled to remove an incorrect image, with no change to text.)

item.title: Russia pledges to continue massive strikes on Kyiv, urges foreign diplomats to leave city
item.description: The campaign is upending life for the capital's 3 million residents ahead of winter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia said on Saturday it would continue to carry out targeted retaliatory strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities and urged foreign nationals and diplomats to leave the capital. In a statement, the Russian Foreign Ministry said that "in response to the Ukrainian Armed Forces' terrorist acts against the civilian population and civilian infrastructure of our country, the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation are continuing to systematically carry out targeted strikes on military facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities". "The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs once again warns foreign nationals, including diplomatic mission staff, against staying in Ukraine or travelling to its territory. "Responsibility for any adverse consequences lies entirely with those who ignore this warning," the ministry said. Russia has recently escalated strikes on infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital, hitting a bridge across the Dnipro river in an air attack on Saturday. The intensifying campaign has [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"upended life"] for the capital's 3 million residents ahead of the bitter winter months. Russian President Vladimir Putin said this week that Ukraine was paying the price for its own attacks on Russia and would continue to do so as Moscow's forces systematically strike different targets there. Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on the other side's grain vessels in the Black Sea in recent months, while Russian oil refineries and other enterprises continue to come under Ukrainian shelling and Ukrainian drones kill civilians in Russian border regions. Both sides deny targeting civilians or civilian infrastructure.

item.title: Decenas de miles de personas se manifiestan en España por la crisis de la vivienda
item.description: Decenas de miles de personas salieron a las calles de Madrid y otras ciudades españolas el sábado para intensificar sus demandas de medidas que aborden la creciente crisis de la vivienda, después de que la oposición rechazara las medidas del Gobierno.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Decenas de miles de personas salieron a las calles de Madrid y otras ciudades españolas el sábado para intensificar sus demandas de medidas que aborden la creciente crisis de la vivienda, después de que la oposición rechazara las medidas del Gobierno. Algunos manifestantes exhibían pancartas en las que se pedía una huelga general después de que el viernes se rechazaran en el Parlamento las medidas elaboradas para dar respuesta a la indignación popular por el desahucio de una mujer de 87 años en Madrid y otros problemas relacionados con la vivienda. "Es una pena", dijo Nando de Anguulo, de 26 años, que se sumó a la protesta del sábado en Madrid. "Esto solo demuestra que somos nosotros, el pueblo, quienes tenemos que adaptarnos a los partidos políticos, y no los políticos a lo que quiere la gente, y esto no puede seguir así". El presidente del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, podría convocar elecciones anticipadas para noviembre tras el rechazo de la legislación, según informaron los medios españoles el viernes, y estaría atento a la intensidad de las protestas del sábado antes de tomar una decisión. La oficina de Sánchez se negó a hacer comentarios sobre estas informaciones. En la ciudad de Valencia, al sureste del país, los manifestantes se enfrentaron el sábado con la policía, que disparó balas de goma y lanzó gases lacrimógenos para dispersar las protestas. Unos 30 manifestantes lograron entrar en la Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias, un emblemático edificio cultural de la ciudad, antes de ser desalojados por la policía. El resto de las manifestaciones, celebradas en 50 ciudades españolas, transcurrieron de forma pacífica. Unas 70.000 personas participaron en la manifestación de Madrid, informó el sábado el Gobierno español.

item.title: US Coast Guard searching for missing jet carrying 6 people bound for Boston
item.description: A private jet has gone missing while traveling to Boston from Bermuda with six people on board, the US Coast Guard said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: A private jet has gone missing while traveling to Boston from Bermuda with six people on board, the US Coast Guard said on Saturday. The Federal Aviation Administration notified the Coast Guard early Saturday that it had lost contact with the plane, a Gulfstream jet used as a medical transfer aircraft, a Coast Guard spokesperson said by email. The Coast Guard said it has dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket, an affluent island community south of mainland Massachusetts. Weather conditions in Nantucket were clear as of Saturday morning according to Accuweather.

item.title: Un ataque israelí en Gaza mata a cinco personas, cuatro de ellas mujeres, dicen autoridades sanitarias
item.description: Un ataque aéreo israelí causó la muerte de al menos cinco palestinos, entre ellos cuatro mujeres, en un edificio de departamentos de la ciudad de Gaza en la madrugada del sábado, informaron responsables de los servicios sanitarios y de defensa civil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un ataque aéreo israelí causó la muerte de al menos cinco palestinos, entre ellos cuatro mujeres, en un edificio de departamentos de la ciudad de Gaza en la madrugada del sábado, informaron responsables de los servicios sanitarios y de defensa civil. Entre los fallecidos se encontraban una madre cristiana y su hija, según los servicios médicos. El ejército israelí no hizo declaraciones de inmediato. El ataque destruyó el bloque de departamentos y provocó un incendio. "Estábamos durmiendo y, de repente, oímos impactos continuos y fuertes explosiones; los niños se despertaron sobresaltados y empezaron a correr y a gritar", explicó el testigo Ahmed Al-Dahdouh. "Salimos corriendo y vimos que la casa de nuestro vecino había sido alcanzada y que había mártires desmembrados, mujeres, hombres y niños; empezamos a sacarlos, estaban esparcidos bajo los escombros", dijo a Reuters. El alto el fuego en Gaza negociado el año pasado por Estados Unidos prevé la reconstrucción final del territorio. Sin embargo, se han logrado pocos avances en la aplicación de un acuerdo para poner fin al conflicto, que incluye condiciones para que Hamás se desarme e Israel retire sus soldados. "Somos musulmanes y estos son nuestros hermanos cristianos, que no tienen nada que ver con nada; son gente pacífica y todo el mundo los quiere, y ahora hemos sacado sus cuerpos, los de una madre y su hija", dijo Dahdouh. Israel, que afirma que Hamás se ha estado rearmando y lanzando ataques en violación del alto el fuego, ha intensificado los ataques contra el grupo en las últimas semanas. Hamás ha negado que intente llevar a cabo ataques o reconstruir su arsenal y acusa a Israel de socavar el acuerdo de paz de Gaza. Las autoridades sanitarias de Gaza han afirmado que al menos 1.400 palestinos han muerto por fuego israelí desde el alto el fuego del pasado mes de octubre. Israel afirma que cuatro de sus soldados han muerto a manos de milicianos en Gaza durante el mismo periodo.

item.title: Portugal prosecutors probe legality of US use of Lajes base in Iran war
item.description: A longstanding agreement with the US allows Washington to use the Azores air base without prior authorization during peacetime, but requires Portugal to give approval once hostilities begin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Portuguese prosecutors said on Saturday they had opened a probe into the legality of the centre-right government's authorisation of the United States' use of the Lajes Air Base in the Azores during the Iran conflict, following a complaint by an opposition party. A longstanding agreement with the US allows Washington to use the base without prior authorisation during peacetime, but requires Portugal to give approval once hostilities begin. Portugal, unlike neighbouring Spain, [USN:L8N3ZS22H TEXT:"authorised several US transit flights"] through the Lajes air base, a decision that drew criticism from left-wing opposition parties and triggered a political debate over Lisbon's role in operations linked to the conflict with Iran. In a statement, the Prosecutor General's Office said "the probe was opened following a complaint filed by members of the Left Bloc party," without providing further details. Portugal's Foreign Ministry declined to comment. The Left Bloc asked prosecutors in April to investigate the US use of the Lajes base, arguing it amounted to a "gross violation of international law." However, Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel has said Portugal was not involved in the conflict and that the use of the Lajes base complied with international law, having been authorised only after assurances from Washington that any operation would be defensive, necessary and proportionate, and limited to military targets. Portugal's prosecutors are bound by the principle of legality, requiring them to investigate alleged wrongdoing when there are sufficient grounds to do so, unlike in some jurisdictions where prosecutors have broader discretion to decide whether a case should proceed. The Lajes base, located in Portugal's Atlantic Azores archipelago, is a strategic transit hub for US forces under a bilateral defence treaty dating back to 1951 and hosts the 65th Air Base Wing of the US Air Force, providing support for US, NATO and allied operations.

item.title: Tens of thousands protest across Spain over housing crisis
item.description: Anger swelled over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her apartment in Madrid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday as they stepped up demands for action to tackle a mounting housing crisis after government measures were struck down by the opposition. Some demonstrators waved posters calling for a general strike after the measures drawn up to address mass anger over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid, and other housing issues, were [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"rejected"] in parliament on Friday. "It's a shame," said Nando de Anguulo, 26, who joined Saturday's protest in Madrid. "It only proves that it is us the people who have to adapt to the political parties, and not the politicians to what the people want, and this can't go on like that." Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez might call a snap election for November after the legislation failed to pass, Spanish media reported on Friday, and would be watching the strength of Saturday's protests before making a decision. Sanchez's office refused to comment on the reports. In the southeastern city of Valencia, demonstrators clashed with police who fired rubber bullets and tear gas to break up protests. About 30 protesters managed to get inside the City of Arts and Sciences, a landmark cultural building in the city, before they were ousted by police. Other demonstrations in 50 Spanish cities were peaceful. Valeria Racu, spokeswoman for the Tenants Union, told reporters in Madrid that a general strike would be called after talks with labour unions. About 70,000 protesters took part in Saturday's demonstration in Madrid, the Spanish government said. Protests planned in Barcelona and the nearby city of Hospitalet de Llobregat were called off because of heavy rain.

item.title: Verstappen consigue su primera pole de la temporada en el GP de Baréin, que se dispuata en Malasia
item.description: Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, se hizo el sábado con su primera pole position de la temporada en el Gran Premio de Fórmula 1 de Baréin, que se celebra en Malasia, demostrando que sigue siendo el dueño del exigente circuito de Sepang nueve años después de su última victoria allí.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
